introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (English Language 1, June 2024, Ordinary/Intermediate Levels, code 0530). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer for each question. The paper has four sections: A listening comprehension (questions 1-10), B reading comprehension (questions 11-25), C grammar (questions 26-40) and D vocabulary (questions 41-50).
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.
incertitudes: Question ouverte (deux options defendables) : Q19 (D parent contre C pastor).

Cles retenues mais moins sures : Q4 (A surprised ; concurrente C frightened), Q10 (A cock intelligent / hare naive ; B et C reposent sur une jalousie commune aux deux), Q16 (B humorous pour 'laughing stock' ; concurrente C pathetic), Q25 (B accepting to follow his friends ; lecture de 'modest reluctance'), Q31 (B lots of information ; C much information est moins naturelle en phrase affirmative), Q34 (D were/would ; B was/would acceptable a l'oral), Q37 (C still yet ; seule option de contraste, tournure rare ; B although concurrente peu logique), Q41 (B infinite ; concurrente C complete).
Q3 : le sujet souligne le e du suffixe -ed de 'accepted' (voyelle /ɪ/) ; la lettre soulignee est precisee dans l'enonce ; la cle est D (sit).
Q48 : l'option B est imprimee 'pretested' (faute pour protested) ; recopiee telle quelle, sans consequence sur la cle D.

Le texte de l'ecoute (Section A) vient des pages d'instructions du professeur, recopie sans les barres obliques de pause et sans les consignes de conduite. Les titres Section One/Two/Three correspondent aux questions 1-3, 4-7 et 8-10 du livret.

Les numeros de ligne des passages de lecture sont repris entre crochets en fin de ligne imprimee (lignes 5, 10, 15... et les lignes citees par les questions : 14 et 29 pour le passage A, 7 pour le passage B). Les mots en gras dans les passages sont les mots ou expressions cites par les questions.

Q47, Q48, Q50 : mots soulignes dans le sujet, rendus en gras Markdown. Les consignes de section (C, D) sont recopiees dans l'enonce de la premiere question de chaque section (Q26, Q41, Q47, Q50) ; la consigne de Q49 ('correctly spelt') est dans son enonce.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Listening passage (read aloud once by the examiner in the real exam - read it once, then answer)**

**Competition can be destructive**

**Section One**

The cock and the hare were once friends. Sooner, they became great rivals given that they were both rich and boastful. They both lived in the same neighbourhood and possessed much livestock. As was the fashion of the time, they both had many wives. Each kept their wives in separate huts. The entire community accepted this kind of family life and the job of each wife was to look after their husband and make their families and farms prosper.

The cock and the hare suddenly became very jealous of each other and feared greatly that each could lure the other's wife away. Like birds of a feather, each person wanted an opportunity to snatch the other's wife. This attitude developed more because the cock wanted to show that he had more money than the hare. The hare in turn wanted to prove stronger than the cock. Above all, he wanted to show that he was smarter. One day, the proud hare visited the cock to steal one of his wives.

**Section Two**

When the hare entered the cock's compound, he saw that the cock was asleep in the shade, with his head tucked under his wings. In amazement at this sight, he cried out in alarm, "Cock, where is your head?" "Oh, I instructed one of my wives to cut it off and place on a high pole in the middle of my compound so that even if I should go on a trip or fall asleep, I can still watch all my wives at once and be satisfied that they do not run off with a lover or with anyone."

He listened to this with rapt attention and decided to move back to his compound and implement what the cock had said because he saw that as a wonderful strategy to protect his wives. He went home and met his eldest wife. The others had gone to the fields for work and to visit friends.

**Section Three**

"Dear wife, take a sharp knife and cut off my head and place it on a pole in the middle of the compound." She was embarrassed and shocked beyond reason. "What is wrong with you and why do you ask me to kill you?" the wife fired back. "Do as I instruct you madam! The cock has tried it and it is working perfectly. Why can't it work with me?" She rightly suspected that the cock could have tricked her husband into committing suicide. "Do as I command, you faithless wretch!" The wife was caught between respect for husband and fear of murder. She went for a very sharp knife and was ready to perform the act. At that moment, a crow came from the back of his house. To the hare's amazement, he saw the cock complete with his head and seemed to smile. "Stop! Don't cut off his head; I wanted to prove to him that birds are wiser animals. I would have allowed him to be killed so that I have access to his wives". In shame, the hare walked into the hut and thought about his foolishness.

**Section A - Listening comprehension (5 marks).** Using only the material read to you from the Listening Comprehension passage, answer each of the following questions as directed. Choose the best answer from the alternatives (A, B, C, D) for each question below.

**Section One**

1. The cock and the hare became rivals because they \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage says they "became great rivals given that they were both rich and boastful". Wealthy and proud restates rich and boastful. Living in the same neighbourhood (B) and owning livestock (A) are only background facts, and they started as friends (D), not as rivals. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: both lived in the same neighborhood

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section One

2. The major cause of suspicion between the two friends was the \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The speaker says the two "feared greatly that each could lure the other's wife away", so each was afraid of losing a wife to the other. Money (A) fed their pride but was not the suspicion; C and D do not describe the fear in the passage. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: fear of losing a wife to the other
fear of being deceived by a wife
fear of one person deceiving the other

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section One

3. You have heard the word 'accepted' read to you from the passage. Choose the word below which has the same vowel sound as the one underlined in accept**e**d (the underlined letter is the **e** of the ending -ed).
questions.corrige_markdown: In "accepted" /ək'septɪd/ the ending -ed is pronounced /ɪd/, so the underlined vowel is the short /ɪ/. "Sit" /sɪt/ has the same vowel. "Ate" has /eɪ/, "life" has /aɪ/ and "test" has /e/ (the vowel of the stressed syllable "cept"), which is the trap. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level English - syllables and sounds

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Two

4. When the hare saw the cock with his head tucked under his wings, he was \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The text says "In amazement at this sight, he cried out": amazement means surprise. He cried out in alarm, but the reaction described first is surprise, and nothing suggests excitement or happiness. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Two

5. The hare went back to his wife after meeting the cock because \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage says he "decided to move back to his compound and implement what the cock had said". He did not challenge the cock (A) or test his wives (C). **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: he wanted to challenge the cock
he wanted to implement what the cock had said
he wanted to put his wives to test
he trusted the cock so well

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Two

6. The expression "... with rapt attention ..." means \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Rapt" means completely absorbed. "Listened with rapt attention" means listened with great interest. "Divided attention" is the opposite. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Two

7. The hare met only one wife at home because \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The passage says "The others had gone to the fields for work and to visit friends." Only C gives both reasons: the fields (farms) and visiting friends. A leaves out the visit, and B merges the two into one place. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the others had gone to the farm
the others had gone to visit friends in the farm
the others had gone to the farms and to visit friends
they had run away in order not to kill the hare

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Three

8. From the instructions given the wife, one can say the hare is \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The hare orders his wife ("Do as I instruct you madam!", "Do as I command"), so he behaves like a dictator: he gives orders and expects obedience. "Dictatorial" describes this style of giving instructions better than the other words. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Three

9. The wife finally went for a knife to cut off the husband's neck \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The wife was "caught between respect for husband and fear of murder" and went for the knife because he commanded her. She had no wish to murder him (A). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: because she wanted to commit murder
for the love she had for her husband
to help her husband protect the other wives

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Listening passage above) Section Three

10. The major difference between the hare and the cock is that \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The cock cleverly tricked the hare with a story he did not need to act out, while the hare naively copied the strategy and was ashamed of his "foolishness". Both were jealous, so B and C do not give a real difference, and the hare is not "liberal". **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: the cock is intelligent while the hare is naive
the cock is jealous while the hare is dishonest
the cock is loving while the hare is jealous
the cock is protective of his wives while the hare is liberal

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section B - Reading comprehension (7½ marks).** Read each passage and answer the questions that follow.

**Passage A - Mind Your Dressing** (questions 11 to 19; the numbers in square brackets are the line numbers printed in the paper, placed at the end of the printed line)

'The way a man dresses is the same way he is addressed', says William Shakespeare.

The human being needs some items to cover the body either for warmth or to avoid being naked. Clothes are basically meant to cover someone's nakedness. With this, one is supposed to dress in such a way that certain strategic parts of the body will not be exposed. Pants, for instance, are meant to cover one's buttocks. Nowadays, this is very far from being the case as buttocks instead cover pants. This is so ironical, isn't it? Today's dressing [5] habits have taken many twists and turns as they have deviated from how they were done in the yesteryears. This is common amongst the youths as they either dress in tattered jeans or miniskirts, thinking that this kind of dressing is "a la mode". It is very common to find boys dressed in tight trousers and T-shirts that expose the shapes of their bodies. Some girls wear blouses that reveal their stomachs and short skirts that expose part of their buttocks. This is **immoral** and can lead to sexual harassment. Some boys wear earrings and plait their hair [10] while girls wear bracelets on their ankles. The plaiting of hair and wearing of earrings are meant for women, not men. Boys who wear earrings think they make them look more elegant or "a la mode", but this is not true. When you are ugly, you are ugly. You just have to accept it.

Talking about being ugly, I don't think there is anyone who is ugly. **Each person is unique** [14] in one way or the other. There are some people who are short, others are tall; some are thin and others are fat. Some are [15] fair, others dark and yet others are brown. All of these are nature's creation and so we do not have to question it. We should learn to dress in a way that matches our various body shapes and sizes.

Bracelets are not meant to be worn on ankles. Necklaces and bracelets are good for adults because they enhance their dressing. What is more embarrassing about these indecent ways of dressing which youths have adopted is that they use them for all occasions and places: churches, schools, parties and even staying at home. [20]

Many youths dress in the manner described above because they feel it is fashionable. They copy these from stars and celebrities like musicians, actors, actresses and even sportsmen. They equally copy from the way people in the Western world dress. Fashion in itself is good but it must be used wisely. There are different clothes for different purposes and occasions. There is a particular style of dressing for work, school, church, parties and so on. A farmer who wears a suit to the farm for instance would be a laughing stock in his [25] community because a suit is formal attire and it is not meant for the farm. In the same way, someone dressed like a star or comedian in normal life looks ridiculous.

Dressing tells a lot about an individual. One's culture can be identified from what one wears. One's style of dressing can also reveal one's **personality** [29]. It can tell if a person is respectable, responsible, humble or proud. [30] While it is important that youths dress in attire that makes them feel happy, it is also necessary to choose the type of dressing that suits the specific occasion. Youths are therefore called upon to dress in accordance with the norms of the societies in which they live.

**Questions 11 to 19**

11. The writer condemns "a la mode" dressing because \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Lines 8-10 call this way of dressing "immoral" and say it "can lead to sexual harassment". The writer never says he is jealous or dislikes stars, and Western fashion is mentioned only as one source of copying. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: it can lead to sexual harassment
it is a western style of dressing

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 12. According to the passage, poor dressing is **im**moral. The underlined portion of the word can be described as a/an \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "im-" is added at the beginning of "moral" to give the opposite meaning, so it is a prefix. A suffix comes at the end and the root is "moral". **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 13. Boys wear earrings because they \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Lines 11-12 say boys "think they make them look more elegant or 'a la mode'". Looking elegant means looking attractive. The writer does not mention competing with women or cost. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: feel it will make them look attractive

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 14. In the expression "each person is unique" (line 14), unique means \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Unique" means one of a kind, different from every other. In the passage each person is "unique in one way or the other", so "special" is the closest. "Common" and "normal" are the opposite, and "equal" would mean the same. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 15. Poor dressing habits are common among \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Line 7 says this is "common amongst the youths". Stars are copied by the youths, and the farmer is only an example of a wrong outfit. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 16. Dressing in a suit to the farm makes some one \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Such a farmer "would be a laughing stock in his community": people laugh at him, so he becomes a humorous (comic) figure. Sarcastic describes someone who mocks, and pathetic and tragic suggest pity or sorrow, not laughter. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 17. The word "personality" (line 29) as used in the passage refers to one's \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence says dressing can reveal one's personality: "respectable, responsible, humble or proud". These are traits of character. Culture is a separate item in the previous sentence. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage A above) 18. According to the passage, to dress well is to look \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The writer wants youths to "dress in accordance with the norms of the societies in which they live" and to suit the occasion: that means looking presentable. He says fashion must be used wisely, and nothing is said about being flashy or expensive. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage A above) 19. The writer of the passage can best be described as \_\_\_\_\_\_.

*Options as printed:* A) researcher   B) satirist   C) pastor   D) parent
questions.corrige_markdown:
The writer advises young people on how to dress, condemns immoral dressing and calls on them to follow the norms of society. He speaks like a caring adult who corrects and guides: "parent" (D) is the most natural choice, and "pastor" (C) is also defensible because of the moral tone and the mention of churches. A satirist (B) would mock society and a researcher (A) would report data, and the passage does neither. Because D and C are both defensible, this question is left open for self-assessment.

**Answer: parent (D) is the best fit; pastor (C) is also defensible.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Passage B - 'Buying the mouth'** (questions 20 to 25; the numbers in square brackets are the line numbers printed in the paper, placed at the end of the printed line)

Late in the night of the third or fourth day, the groom's friends escort him to his bride. It is expected that he should show some kind of modest reluctance. When they get to the room they will find the bride sitting all alone with her head well covered. She does not say a word to them and does not even acknowledge their presence. The custom requires that her speech has to be bought or what the Hausas call 'buying the mouth'. [5] The groom himself does not say a word in the proceedings that follow.

The friends try to make her speak or laugh by making jokes or telling funny stories, but **this is always futile** [7]. Then negotiations for her speech begin. They name a sum as a price for her speech, beginning from a fairly low figure. She shakes her head from side to side to signify 'nothing doing'. Then they name a higher figure and again she shakes her head from side to side to show non-acceptance.

The bargaining continues until **she nods her head up and down to signify assent** [10]. The sum is then paid by the friends and the bride can now talk to them. After further conversation for about half an hour, the friends withdraw leaving the bride and groom together. The bridegroom makes a modest attempt to follow them, but the door is closed before he can get out. He is then expected to stay with his bride for a few minutes, but to join his friends again. They talk for a while and then bid each other good night. The groom comes back [15] and sleeps in his room with his bride.

**Questions 20 to 25**

20. The bride remains silent when the groom's friends enter her room because \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Lines 4-5 say custom requires "her speech has to be bought" ('buying the mouth'). Being alone and the late hour are only the setting, and the groom's silence is not the cause of hers. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: they have visited her late in the night
it is expected that they have to buy her speech
the groom himself does not say a word

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage B above) 21. In the expression "this is always futile" (line 7), the word 'futile' is a/an \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Futile" (useless, without result) follows the verb "is" and describes "this", so it is an adjective. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage B above) 22. According to the passage the bride begins to speak when \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Lines 10-11: "The sum is then paid by the friends and the bride can now talk to them." The friends, not the groom, pay, and naming a price is not enough: it must be paid. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: the groom names a high enough price
the groom pays a price acceptable to her
the friends pay a price acceptable to her
his friends name a high enough price

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage B above) 23. The bride indicates that the price for her speech is too low by \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Lines 8-9: when the price is low "she shakes her head from side to side" to show non-acceptance. She never speaks (B), and nodding means acceptance. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: shaking her head from side to side
nodding her head up and down
simply waiting motionless till a higher price is named

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage B above) 24. In the expression "she nods her head up and down to signify assent" (line 10), 'assent' means \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: To nod the head up and down means "yes", so assent is agreement or acceptance. Refusal, objection and dislike all mean the opposite. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: (Passage B above) 25. According to the passage the groom pretends to show reluctance to receive his bride by \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: Lines 1-2 say he "should show some kind of modest reluctance" and lines 12-13 explain how: when the friends leave, "the bridegroom makes a modest attempt to follow them". So he shows reluctance by trying to follow his friends out instead of staying. Nothing is said about looking at the bride or about low payment. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: letting his friends offer low payment
refusing to look at the bride
permitting his friends to accompany him

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section C - Grammar (7½ marks).** Read the instructions for each question before answering. For numbers 26 - 40, choose the answer that best completes each sentence.

26. Since Namondo takes \_\_\_\_\_\_ her mother, you can be sure of her strictness.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Take after" is a phrasal verb meaning to resemble a family member in character. Takes up, takes on and takes from do not give this meaning. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 27. The principal couldn't have said a thing like that, \_\_\_\_\_\_?
questions.corrige_markdown: A question tag repeats the auxiliary of the main clause with the opposite polarity. The clause "couldn't have said" is negative with the auxiliary "could", so the tag is the positive "could he?". **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 28. \_\_\_\_\_\_ and \_\_\_\_\_\_ are living in the same street.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both words are the subject of "are living", so subject pronouns are needed: "I", not "me". Politeness puts the other person first: "Rose and I". **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 29. In the sentence "Okie's brother has a tamed lion in Kumba", tamed is a/an \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Tamed" is a past participle used before the noun "lion" to describe it, so it functions as an adjective. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 30. Had it rained heavily this morning, I \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Had it rained" is an inverted third conditional (= If it had rained), so the result clause takes "would have + past participle": "I wouldn't have travelled". The other options are not grammatical. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 31. Newspapers today carry \_\_\_\_\_\_ about the president's visit.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Information" is uncountable, so it has no plural (A and D are wrong). "Much" is normally avoided in affirmative sentences, where "lots of" or "a lot of" is used, so B is the standard answer. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level English - countable and uncountable nouns

questions.enonce_markdown: 32. "Show me the way to church", the new pastor requested. In reported speech, it is correct to say The new pastor \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: A request is reported with a reporting verb such as "asked for" and no quotation marks. A and D keep the direct speech, and C changes the meaning. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: said show me the way to church
asked for the way to church
asked, "show me the way to church"

questions.enonce_markdown: 33. Even though Jonas was unemployed, he turned \_\_\_\_\_\_ the post of a mortuary attendant.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Turn down" means to refuse. The "even though" clause shows that it is surprising he refused the job. "Turned up" means arrived, "turned in" means went to bed or handed in. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 34. If she \_\_\_\_\_\_ my sister I \_\_\_\_\_\_ talk to her about it this evening.
questions.corrige_markdown: This is a second (unreal) conditional: "If + past subjunctive (were), would + base verb". "Were" is the standard form for all persons in this structure. "Was/would" is heard in informal speech, but the Board expects "were". **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 35. Kimberly lives in a \_\_\_\_\_\_ house.
questions.corrige_markdown: Adjectives follow the order opinion, age, colour: beautiful (opinion), new (age), green (colour). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 36. The correct form of the passive voice "Kate had built the house before her husband married her" is: That house \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: The active past perfect "had built" becomes "had been built" in the passive, and "her husband married her" becomes "she was married to her husband". B uses the present perfect and C loses the past perfect. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: had been built by Kate before she was married to her husband
has been built by Kate before she was married to her husband
was built by Kate before she was married to her husband
had to be built by Kate before she had to be married to her husband

questions.enonce_markdown: 37. He usually came late to school, \_\_\_\_\_\_ he succeeded in his end of course examination.
questions.corrige_markdown: The two ideas contrast: he was late, but he still succeeded. "Consequently" and "therefore" show result, which does not fit, and "although" would reverse the logic of a sentence that starts with the main idea. "Still yet" is the only option that expresses contrast after a comma. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 38. Students who take their studies \_\_\_\_\_\_ always succeed.
questions.corrige_markdown: The verb phrase "take their studies" is modified by an adverb, "seriously". The other options are adjectives. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 39. I \_\_\_\_\_\_ smoking only last week and I \_\_\_\_\_\_ to feel better already.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Only last week" requires the simple past ("quit"). "Already" with a present result gives the present continuous: "I am beginning to feel better". A, B and D mix tenses wrongly. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 40. Each of the boys \_\_\_\_\_\_ four books.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Each" is singular, so the verb is singular, and "have" (possession) is not used in the continuous: "Each of the boys has four books". **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Section D - Vocabulary (5 marks).** Read the instructions for each question or set of questions carefully before answering. For numbers 41 - 46, choose the answer that best completes each sentence.

41. A mother's love for her child is \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: A mother's love is said to have no limit, which is expressed by "infinite". Compulsory and demanding do not fit love, and "complete" is weaker. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: 42. Many think that politics is a game of interest because politicians have no \_\_\_\_\_\_.
questions.corrige_markdown: A conscience is the inner sense of right and wrong. People who act only in their own interest are said to have no conscience. Consciousness means awareness, which is the confusable word. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: 43. He scored low marks in the exam because of his \_\_\_\_\_\_ knowledge of the subject.
questions.corrige_markdown: Low marks come from knowledge that is shallow, "superficial". Deep and thorough knowledge would give high marks. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: 44. Bees are always \_\_\_\_\_\_ in flower gardens.
questions.corrige_markdown: Bees make a "buzzing" sound. Growl, roar and hiss belong to other animals. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: 45. Most earth roads are often \_\_\_\_\_\_ passable in the raining season.
questions.corrige_markdown: The prefix im- is used before words beginning with p (impassable); un-, dis- and in- do not form "impassable". **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: 46. The \_\_\_\_\_\_ of his life is so complicated; one can't really follow it.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Course of his life" means the way his life has gone. "Coarse" (rough) sounds the same but has a different meaning. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown:
**For numbers 47 - 48, choose the answer that best explains the meaning of the underlined word.**

47. Many people admire Mr and Mrs Nubed for being a __welcoming__ couple.
questions.corrige_markdown: A welcoming couple receive guests warmly, which is "hospitable". Sociable means fond of company, which is not the same. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level English - synonyms and antonyms
O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: 48. Even advocates of war __lamented__ the loss of lives in the crisis.
questions.corrige_markdown: To lament is to feel or show deep sorrow, which is "grieved". Opposed and rejected mean the opposite of accepting, and "pretested" is a printing error for "protested", which would not fit either. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level English - synonyms and antonyms
O Level English - vocabulary in context

questions.enonce_markdown: 49. Choose the word that is correctly spelt.

**Choose the answer that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word.**

50. Someone sent an __anonymous__ letter to me.
questions.corrige_markdown: Anonymous means without a name. The opposite is "identified" (the sender is named). "Nameless" and "sourceless" are synonyms. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level English - synonyms and antonyms
